'''Katalin Marton''' (9 December 1941 &ndash; 13 December 2019) was a Hungarian mathematician, born in Budapest.
==Education and career==
Marton obtained her PhD from [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in 1965 and worked at the Department of Numerical Mathematics, Central Research Institute for Physics, Budapest from 1965 to 1973. Important influences on her early career were her attendance at the combinatorics seminar organised by [[Alfréd Rényi]] from 1966, meeting [[Roland Dobrushin]] in Debrecen in 1967 (which led to her visiting the Institute for Problems in Information Transmission in Moscow in 1969<ref>{{cite web|url=http://isl.stanford.edu/~abbas/presentations/Marton.pdf|title=Katalin Marton|first=Abbas|last=El Gamal|author-link=Abbas El Gamal|work=Withits 2010|year=2010|publisher=Stanford University|access-date=2019-12-18|archive-date=2023-11-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114040342/http://isl.stanford.edu/~abbas/presentations/Marton.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>), and her collaboration with [[Imre Csiszár]] which began in 1972. From 1973 she worked at the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics]] of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in [[Budapest]], visiting the United States in 1977 (for the [[IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory|International Symposium on Information Theory]] in Ithaca) and in 1979–80 (meeting [[Robert Gallager]] at MIT and [[Robert M. Gray]] at Stanford).

==Research interests==
Marton worked on various areas of mathematics, including [[information theory]], [[concentration of measure]] and [[probability theory]]. In a 1974 paper on information theory she used a combinatorics approach to characterize error in discrete memoryless sources under distortion.<ref name="ieeee-itsn"/> She was particularly well known for her two-page proof, based on an information-theoretic coupling inequality, of the blowing-up lemma,<ref>
{{Cite journal
| volume = 32
| issue = 3
| pages = 445–446
| last = Marton
| first = K.
 | title = A simple proof of the blowing-up lemma (Corresp.)
| journal = IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
| year = 1986
| doi=10.1109/TIT.1986.1057176
}}
</ref> published in 1986. This result, which arose out of work of [[Grigory Margulis]] in 1974<ref>
{{cite journal
|last = Margulis
|first = G. A.
|title = Probabilistic characteristics of graphs with large connectivity
|journal = Problemy Peredachi Informatsii
|volume = 10
|number =2
|pages = 101–108
|year = 1974
}}</ref> and which was developed further by [[Rudolf Ahlswede]], Peter Gács and [[János Körner]],<ref>
{{cite journal
|last = Ahlswede
|first = R.
|author2 = P. Gács
|author3 = J. Körner
|title = Bounds on conditional probabilities with applications in multi-user communication
|journal = Z. Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie Verw. Gebiete
|volume = 34
|number = 3
|pages = 157–177
|year = 1976
|doi= 10.1007/BF00535682
|s2cid = 13901122
|doi-access = free
}}</ref> shows that (in product measures) the neighbourhood of a set of greater than exponentially small size has size close to 1. This result is used in a variety of contexts including strong converse results for coding theorems, classification and model selection.

Marton was also responsible for the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture,<ref>Blogpost by [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Green]] https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2007/03/11/ben-green-the-polynomial-freiman-ruzsa-conjecture/</ref> a central question of [[additive combinatorics]], now also called [[Freiman's theorem]]. This was published by [[Imre Z. Ruzsa|Imre Ruzsa]] but as he mentions<ref>
{{cite journal
|first = I.
|last = Ruzsa
|title = An analog of Freiman's theorem in groups
|journal = Astérisque
|volume = 258
|year = 1999
|pages = 323–326
|url = http://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1999__258__323_0.pdf}}</ref>
this conjecture came from Marton. It states that if a subset <math>A</math> of a group <math>G</math> (a power of a [[cyclic group]]) has small [[Additive combinatorics#Doubling constant|doubling constant]] then <math>A</math> lies in the union of a bounded polynomial number of cosets of some subgroup <math>H</math>. This conjecture is deeply characteristic to the way Marton fed back particular information-theoretic results into the mainstream of mathematics. In 2012 [[Tom Sanders (mathematician)|Tom Sanders]] gave an almost polynomial bound of the conjecture for abelian groups.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sanders |first=Tom |date=2012-10-15 |title=On the Bogolyubov–Ruzsa lemma |url=http://msp.org/apde/2012/5-3/p05.xhtml |journal=Analysis & PDE |language=en |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=627–655 |doi=10.2140/apde.2012.5.627 |issn=1948-206X|doi-access=free |arxiv=1011.0107 }}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 2023 a solution over <math>G=\mathbb F_2^n</math> a field of characteristic 2 has been posted as a preprint by [[Timothy Gowers|Tim Gowers]], [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Green]], Freddie Manners and [[Terence Tao|Terry Tao]].<ref>{{Cite arXiv|last1=Gowers |first1=W. T. |last2=Green |first2=Ben |last3=Manners |first3=Freddie |last4=Tao |first4=Terence |date=2023 |title=On a conjecture of Marton |class=math.NT |eprint=2311.05762}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sloman |first=Leila |date=2023-12-06 |title='A-Team' of Math Proves a Critical Link Between Addition and Sets |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-team-of-math-proves-a-critical-link-between-addition-and-sets-20231206/ |access-date=2023-12-11 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

Marton's other major contributions included coding theorems for the broadcast channel<ref>
{{cite journal
|first = K.

}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal

|journal = IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
|volume = 23
|number =1
|pages = 60–64
|year = 1977
|doi= 10.1109/TIT.1977.1055655}}</ref> (with the former paper proving the best-known inner bound on the capacity region of the two-receiver general broadcast channel, often referred to as "Marton's inner bound"<ref>{{cite journal
|last = Gohari
|first = A.A. 
|author2 = V. Anantharam
|year = 2012
|title = Evaluation of Marton's inner bound for the general broadcast channel
|journal = IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
|volume = 58
|number = 2
|doi = 10.1109/TIT.2011.2169537
|arxiv = 1006.5166 
|pages = 608–619|s2cid = 415264 
}}</ref>)
and many other results in concentration of measure,<ref>
{{cite journal
|last = Marton
|first = K.
|year = 1996
|title = Bounding <math>\bar{d}</math>-distance by informational divergence: A method to prove measure concentration
|journal = Annals of Probability
|volume = 24
|number = 2 
|pages = 857–866
|doi= 10.1214/aop/1039639365
|doi-access = free
}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|first = K.
|last = Marton

|journal = Annals of Probability
|number = 3B
|pages = 2526–2544
|title = Measure concentration for Euclidean distance in the case of dependent random variables
|doi = 10.1214/009117904000000702
|volume = 32
|year = 2004
|arxiv = math/0410168|bibcode = 2004math.....10168M|doi-access = free
}}</ref> [[rate-distortion theory]]<ref>{{cite journal 
|first = K. 
|last = Marton
|title = Asymptotic behavior of the rate distortion function of discrete stationary processes
|journal = Problemy Peredachi Informatsii
|volume = VII
|number = 2
|pages = 3–14
|year = 1971}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
|first = K. 
|last = Marton
|title = On the rate distortion function of stationary sources
|journal = Problems of Control and Information Theory
|volume = 4
|pages = 289–297
|year = 1975}}</ref> and graph capacity.<ref>{{cite journal
|first = J.
|last = Körner
|author2 = K. Marton
|title = Random access communication and graph entropy
|journal = IEEE Transactions on Information Theory
|volume = 34
|number = 2
|pages = 312–314 
|year = 1988
|doi =  10.1109/18.2639}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal
|first = K. 
|last = Marton
|title = On the Shannon capacity of probabilistic graphs
|journal = Journal of Combinatorial Theory
|volume = 57
|issue = 2
|pages = 183–195
|year  = 1993
|doi = 10.1006/jctb.1993.1015|doi-access = free
}}</ref> Marton had an [[Erdős number]] of 2, for example via her collaboration<ref>{{cite journal
|first = I.
|last = Csiszár
|author2 = J. Körner
|author3= L. Lovász
|author4 = K. Marton
|author5=  G. Simonyi
|title= Entropy splitting for antiblocking corners and perfect graphs
|journal= Combinatorica
|year= 1990
|volume=10
|number=1
|pages=27–40
|doi=10.1007/BF02122693|s2cid = 16508298
}}</ref> with [[Imre Csiszár]] and [[László Lovász]].

==Awards and recognition==
In 1996, Marton won the [[Alfréd Rényi Prize]] from the Alfréd Rényi Institute. In 2013, she was the first (and so far only) female winner of the [[Claude E. Shannon Award]], the top prize in [[information theory]], from the [[IEEE]]. As a result, she delivered the Shannon Lecture at the International Symposium on Information Theory in Istanbul in 2013, with her talk being entitled <em>Distance-Divergence Inequalities</em>.<ref>Slides of 2013 Shannon lecture https://www.itsoc.org/resources/videos/isit-2013-istanbul/MartonISIT2013.pdf/view {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218120851/https://www.itsoc.org/resources/videos/isit-2013-istanbul/MartonISIT2013.pdf/view |date=2019-12-18 }}</ref><ref>Video of 2013 Shannon Lecture: https://vimeo.com/135256376</ref><ref>Blogpost about 2013 Shannon Lecture: https://infostructuralist.wordpress.com/2013/07/29/isit-2013-two-plenaries-on-concentration-of-measure/</ref> The citation and biographical sketch<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://media.itsoc.org/marton-interview.pdf |title=Interview with Katalin Marton - Shannon Award Winner 2013 - Archived copy |access-date=2019-12-18 |archive-date=2018-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201014426/http://media.itsoc.org/marton-interview.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> paid tribute to her scientific contributions, with Fields Medallist [[Cédric Villani]] writing:
<blockquote>
"Marton is one of the leading authorities about the applications of information theory techniques to concentration theory, in particular in the setting of [[Markov chain|Markov Chains]]. Most importantly, in the mid-nineties, Marton pointed out the interest and importance of entropy inequalities in the study of the concentration phenomena. Talagrand has acknowledged the influence of Marton in this respect, and this motivated him to establish the famous [[Michel Talagrand|Talagrand]] inequality<ref>{{cite journal
|last = Talagrand
|first = M.
|title= Transportation cost for Gaussian and other product measures
|journal= Geometric and Functional Analysis
|year= 1996
|volume=6
|number=3
|pages=587–600
|doi=10.1007/BF02249265|s2cid = 120778404
}} (note paper Acknowledgement "The author is grateful to Professor Marton for sending him her paper which motivated this work")</ref> controlling the [[Wasserstein metric|Wasserstein distance]] by the square root of the [[Entropy (information theory)|Boltzmann-Shannon information]]. In turn, the Talagrand inequality triggered the development a whole field, which I explored with [[Felix Otto (mathematician)|Otto]], [[Robert McCann (mathematician)|McCann]], [[John Lott (mathematician)|Lott]] and others, involving entropy, concentration, [[Transportation theory (mathematics)|transport]], [[Ricci curvature]], with very far reaching geometric consequences."
</blockquote>

In 2013, Marton was also awarded the {{ill|József Eötvös Wreath|hu|Eötvös József-koszorú}} by the [[Hungarian Academy of Science]].<ref name="renyi_death" />
